subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: How should managed Memory Dreaming surface partial workspace failures or no-op `NO_REPLY` runs in cron status and diagnostics?
rationale: Current code can preserve an outer handled cron result while memory-core records failed workspaces locally, and changing that status semantics affects cron UX, doctor checks, and existing automation expectations.

options.title: Define degraded cron status
options.body: Keep the issue open and choose an explicit degraded/error/diagnostic status path for Dreaming runs that do not advance any workspace or have per-workspace failures.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Keep cron status `ok` but require doctor and Dreaming-specific diagnostics to report stale ingestion/diary state and failed workspace counts.

options.title: Close after live proof
options.body: Close only if a fresh current-release deployment proves Dreaming ingestion, diary output, and cron state now advance and no status gap remains.

recommendation.title: Define degraded cron status
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and choose an explicit degraded/error/diagnostic status path for Dreaming runs that do not advance any workspace or have per-workspace failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent SQLite state migration and memory-state repair work makes this the closest available owner for deciding how current state and diagnostics should represent the remaining Dreaming failure class.
